abstract: In 1965, Bregman proved that the sequence of iterates of the method of alternating projections applied to two closed convex sets with nonempty intersection in a Hilbert space converges weakly to a point in the intersection. The question whether this convergence may actually fail to be strong was settled in a seminal paper by Hundal in 2004. He provided a counterexample featuring a halfspace and a closed convex cone generated by a certain curve. While largely elementary, the details of Hundal's construction and analysis are quite involved. We revisit this seminal example and present a family of such examples that allows for simpler proofs. Our generating curve combines unit vectors with Gaussian inner products and a height determined by a scalar function. The orbits converge weakly --- but not strongly --- to the origin, while their norms have a positive limit for which we give explicit lower bounds. We also prove that the associated Ces\`aro means behave likewise; in fact, this is generalized to alternating proximal mappings whose composition has a fixed point. Finally, these orbits allow interpretations in the context of projected-gradient, proximal-point, and gradient-descent algorithms.
hook: A simpler family of examples shows alternating projections can converge weakly but never strongly.
summary: The authors build a new family of examples, simpler than Hundal's 2004 counterexample, in which alternating projections between a halfspace and a cone converge weakly to the origin while the norms stay bounded away from zero. Explicit lower bounds on those norms are given, and the same failure holds for Cesaro means and alternating proximal maps. It is a purely theoretical result in infinite-dimensional Hilbert space.
title: A family of alternating projection examples whose Ces\`aro means fail to converge strongly
